meta.title: WoW Forever Druid spell ranks, every level 1-60

status_legend.forever: Forever client data (build 1.60.1.70862) as carried by wowsims-forever

source.records: sim/core/spelldata/spells_auto_gen.go (wowsims's generator bakes in tools/database/overrides; any override comment is copied to the rank's wowsims_overrides: those fields are wowsims's in-game measurements, not client rows)
source.vanilla: cmangos classic-db spell_template (1.12) for vanilla_* fields, npc_trainer_template 111 + npc_trainer rows of class 11 trainers for vanilla_trainer (teach spell -> learned spell through effect 36 LEARN_SPELL)

formulas.value_at_level: BasePoints + PPL * clamp(min(L, scaling_max_level) - scaling_base_level, 0); scaling_max_level 0 = no cap. Computed in float32 as wowsims Effect.AverageAt. Damage/heal amounts keep the fraction; every other amount is floored.
formulas.cost: cost.mana flat; cost.pct_base_mana = pct of base mana (base_mana table in <class>_levels.json); cost.rage in rage (row value / 10); cost.energy; cost.combo_points_min = the finisher needs at least that many; cost.health (Life Tap row has none: wowsims spends amount + Spirit).
formulas.learn_level: SpellLevels.SpellLevel of the rank (client). learned_from.vanilla_trainer gives the vanilla 1.12 trainer level and cost for comparison. 2 Nov notes: training every class ability 1-60 costs 206-207 gold in Forever, so vanilla costs are not Forever costs.
formulas.vanilla_compare: vanilla.changes_vs_vanilla compares learn level, flat cost, cooldowns and each effect's amount at the learn level (vanilla BasePoints+1 .. BasePoints+DieSides, Forever tooltip range) with the 1.12 row of the same id. A difference of 1 point or less is ignored. Cast times and durations are not compared (the 1.12 rows store index ids into tables not in the local data).
formulas.required_stance_mask: client StanceMask bit field (1 << (form id - 1)); e.g. warrior Battle 17, Defensive 18, Berserker 19; druid Cat 1, Bear 5, Dire Bear 8, Moonkin 31.

coefficient_penalties.finding: Neither wowsims-forever nor mythicsim-forever-engine applies the vanilla sub-20 penalty (1 - (20 - spellLevel)*0.0375) or a downrank coefficient penalty. Ranks learned below 20 carry sp_coef_if_vanilla_sub20_penalty so a sim can switch the vanilla rule on.
coefficient_penalties.forever_notes: kami-labs summary of the 2 Nov 2026 notes: the low-rank penalty was removed from several chance-based talents and stays on Arcane Concentration, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost (proc less often when the rank was learned more than 12 levels below the caster). Nothing in the notes speaks to damage/heal coefficients of low ranks.

forever_class_notes: Nature's Grasp baseline (10), Revive (12), Omen of Clarity baseline (20), Lacerate baseline (42); forms keep weapon DPS (cat 1.0 s, bear 2.5 s), consumables and weapon enchants work in form; Tiger's Fury removed (deep dive).
2 Nov notes: Bear threat 115%, Shred 200% / Claw 140% / Ravage 435% weapon damage, Rip/Rake/Bite/Pounce +25%, Starfire +40%, new Ferocious Bite rank 1 at 24, Poised at 32.
notes_sources: Warcraft Tavern summaries of Blizzard's Forever class deep dives: Priest & Warrior (1 Oct 2026, Blizzard news 24301514), Mage & Shaman (7 Oct, 24302097), Rogue & Warlock (7 Oct, 24310968); 'All Changes to Paladins' (21 Sep 2026); 'WoW Forever Pre-Launch Class Changes & Bug Fixes' (4 Nov 2026, from Kaivax's Beta Development Notes updated 2 Nov).
Blizzard news 'World of Warcraft: Forever Class Deep Dives - Hunter and Druid' (news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24301515).
kami-labs 'WoW Forever November 2 patch: 223 changes before launch' (datamined items marked).
The Blizzard forum dev-notes thread itself could not be fetched here (needs approval); its content is taken from the summaries above.
Where a note and a client row disagree, the row wins; the row values are the ones in ranks[].

BearForm.name: Bear Form
notes: Learned at 10. BearFormTriggered (1178): armor +180%, max health 20+18/level (10-40), AP 30+3/level (10-40). 4 Nov notes: Bear/Dire Bear threat bonus 50% -> 115%.

wowsims_code_notes.comment: Dire Bear keeps the bear bit so a bear-only cast and InForm(Bear) both match. The shapeshift aura's misc value is the game files' form id. SpellShapeshiftForm.DamageVariance is 0.4 for Cat, Bear, and Dire Bear. The paw uses the weapon's table DPS and form variance, with single-precision endpoints rounded before AP and flat enchant or stone damage. TODO: Ingame test needed -- whether the paw also takes the QualityModifier the table DPS leaves out. A bear's auto attack takes the two-hander rage factor: a combat log shows 11.25 rage a swing at the bear's 2.5 seconds, 4.5 rage per second of swing. No druid row states a rage multiplier of its own. TODO: Ingame test needed -- whether a bear holding a one-hander takes the one-hand factor instead, and whether a bear's crit doubles the whole swing as a two-hand warrior's does (measured on warriors only). Bear Form (Passive2) 21178 holds the bear forms' threat, an A_MOD_THREAT on every school. Neither form's row names it, so the store carries it as an extra spell. Out of the APL with its spell, which Dire Bear Form replaces. Armor from items, base and bonus, health, attack power and the Faerie Fire spell mods are parsed. TODO: Ingame research needed -- effect 4 of Bear Form and Dire Bear Form is aura 668, which core does not name. A swing replacement also asks the rotation to queue an attack before the swing. Only Bear forms can queue Maul. A change of form keeps the health percentage while the forms' health and Stamina move the maximum. It wraps the forms' handlers whole, so it runs in Initialize, after the talents have attached theirs. Dire Bear Form replaces Bear Form once learned, at level 40. A shift into Bear or Dire Bear Form starts the rage bar at 0, and Furor's rage comes on top. The starting form is not cast, so the pull keeps the starting rage. TODO: Verify a companion-triggered swing reset before adding a snake-weaving option. The rage chance, the tooltip's $m1: 0.2 at 1/5 through 1 at 5/5. Bear forms preserve the stored energy and pause regeneration until the form ends. The tooltip's rule, priced with $m2: the energy left in Cat Form plus ${10*($m2/100)} for each second spent outside Bear Form or Dire Bear Fo

Enrage.name: Enrage

cost.rage_note: rage costs are stored x10 in the row; shown here in rage

notes: Deep dive: generates 10 initial rage.

wowsims_code_notes.comment: The tooltip's "reduces base armor by 27% in Bear Form and 16% in Dire Bear Form". The row carries the penalty as effect 4, an A_DUMMY with no value. Base armor is the equipment share.

TODO: Faerie Fire does not reset the swing timer. TODO: Ingame research needed: Faerie Fire's threat in Bear and Dire Bear Form; its E_THREAT effect states 0. The timer must exist before the form passive adds its recovery time. Cost, cooldown and GCD in cat or bear come from the form passive's spell mods. A cast on a target that has the debuff refreshes it; when to refresh is the rotation's.

A landed caster-form debuff can roll it without dealing damage. One Hurricane tick rolls once however many targets it lands on; the first target to reach the condition takes the roll. Chance(1) keeps the resolver from building a procs-per-minute manager and leaves core no roll of its own. The chance depends on what hit, so it is drawn here, after the ICD check and before the ICD starts. Only auto attacks and druid spells roll it. The 15 October development notes take Faerie Fire cast in Cat, Bear or Dire Bear Form off Omen of Clarity. No row states it.

Innervate.name: Innervate
notes: Mana return (spirit regen multiplier, row).

wowsims_code_notes.comment: Every raid player can receive Innervate; RegisterAura cannot run after finalize. A friendly APL target receives the mana. Cast Spell aims at the encounter, so the dest is InnervateTarget or the caster.

Binary: the row's second effect lowers the target's chance to hit, and a spell with a non-damage effect is resisted whole or not at all. wowsims_code_notes.comment: The October 8 hotfixes: "Shifting Power can no longer be used while already at Full Energy." The rows state no such rule.

The energy the cat can spend now without delaying a coming Rip or Rake refresh.  A refresh counts when its bleed is up and the fight lasts long enough after it runs out for a new one to be worth casting: Rip at 5 combo points with 10s of fight left, Rake with a full Rake left. Taking the refreshes in time order, the energy regenerated before each one pays for it; what regeneration cannot cover has to be kept from now. The result is the current energy minus what has to be kept. The first refresh after Shifting Power is ready costs Shifting Power's energy less. When Shifting Power gives more than that refresh costs, the cost goes below zero and the energy left over goes to the next refresh.
